title: Tight Quarter-Wave Initialization with Gradient Constraints
scientific_hypothesis: Confining thickness optimization to ±4 nm around quarter-wave optical targets at 1550 nm, with adjacent-layer gradient penalty |t_i - t_{i+1}| ≤ 12 nm, will prevent rapid phase drift that caused score regression while preserving constructive interference in the passband.
design_principle: Quarter-wave DBR with defect cavity structure, initialized at nH*dH = nL*dL = 1550/4 nm optical thickness, with tight bounds to maintain optimizer in constructive-interference basin.
proposed_topology: 20-layer alternating Ta2O5/SiO2 stack starting with Ta2O5 on air side, terminating with SiO2 on fused silica substrate. Exact sequence: Air|Ta2O5|SiO2|Ta2O5|SiO2|Ta2O5|SiO2|Ta2O5|SiO2|Ta2O5|SiO2|Ta2O5|SiO2|Ta2O5|SiO2|Ta2O5|SiO2|Ta2O5|SiO2|Ta2O5|SiO2|Fused Silica
design_variables: layer thicknesses with ±4 nm bounds around quarter-wave targets
manufacturing_considerations: tight thickness bounds improve fabrication repeatability
gradient constraint reduces stress from rapid thickness changes
theory_basis: Quarter-wave optical thickness n*d = lambda0/4 creates maximum reflectance in DBR mirrors
Defect layer with half-wave optical thickness creates transmission peak in stopband
expected_advantages: Prevents optimizer from drifting into destructive interference regions
Maintains proximity to proven quarter-wave design principle
known_risks: Tight bounds may prevent optimizer from finding global optimum
May not fully recover round 1 performance if quarter-wave initialization is suboptimal
execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer planar dielectric filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Materials: Ta2O5 (high index) and SiO2 (low index), alternating starting with Ta2O5. Initialize all Ta2O5 layers at quarter-wave optical thickness for 1550 nm (approximately 157 nm physical thickness assuming n≈2.45), all SiO2 layers at quarter-wave optical thickness for 1550 nm (approximately 267 nm assuming n≈1.46). Apply optimization bounds of ±4 nm around these quarter-wave targets. Add hard penalty constraint on adjacent-layer thickness gradients: |t_i - t_{i+1}| ≤ 12 nm for all adjacent pairs. Add lightweight stochastic offsets ≤2 nm to preserve asymmetry. Optimize for maximum transmittance at 1550 nm (single wavelength), minimum mean transmittance across 1400-1500 nm band, minimum mean transmittance across 1600-1700 nm band. Total layer count fixed at 20. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with these constraints. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1400-1500 nm, 1550-1550 nm, 1600-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance at 1550 nm (soft target ≥ 0.95); strong suppression of transmittance in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 1400-1500 nm; transmittance in 1600-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30.
revision_reason: Direct response to feedback directive: initialize with thicknesses locked within ±4 nm of quarter-wave optical targets, add hard penalty on adjacent-layer thickness gradients ≤12 nm, retain lightweight stochastic offsets ≤2 nm to preserve asymmetry hypothesis while keeping optimizer confined to constructive-interference basin.
